metadata.note: The West Virginia and Pittsburgh Railroad (Clarksburg - Weston - Burnsville - Flatwoods - Camden-on-Gauley, with the Sutton branch and the Weston - Buckhannon - Pickens (Newlon) branch; Senator J. N. Camden's road) and its Baltimore and Ohio successor service after the 31 Aug 1899 lease, including the B&O's 1901 extension Camden-on-Gauley - Richwood. Drawn from research/branches/west_virginia_and_pittsburgh_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (2026-10-27). Before this layer the map drew none of this road. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn; they keep to years a source confirms. Rule 4 split at the 31 Aug 1899 lease: WV&P features 1890-1899 in the WV&P's own colour, B&O features from 1899 in the B&O colour, on identical geometry for every corridor that ran in both eras. The 1912 corporate merger (or 1990 CSX merger, per abandonedonline) changed no operator and is not a split. Mileposts are Fowler's, from Clarksburg (table 18) and Weston (table 20).
sources: Fowler, West Virginia Railroads SL 227 (18.02.22), https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/westvirginiarrs.pdf, tables 18-20
Busy Bee (Buckhannon), Webster Echo (Addison), Clarksburg Telegram and other Chronicling America newspapers, https://www.loc.gov/collections/chronicling-america/ (individual issues cited per segment)
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (schedules of 30 Sept 1951), Tables 37, 38 and 54
metadata.geometry_method: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) plus OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) for lifted grades, traced with opstrace.py: Dijkstra over all railway ways; ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O WITHOUT a note:old_railway_operator (OSM marks the ex-Coal and Coke and Strouds Creek & Muddlety track with that note), and OHM ways named West Virginia & Pittsburg Railroad / Buckhannon & West Fork / Buckhannon River Railroad / Sutton Branch or with operator B&O, costed 1x; untagged rail 1.25x; OHM 'Cowen Subdivision' 2x; cycleways 3x; any other named operator, any B&O way noted as another predecessor, and named neighbouring roads (Coal & Coke, Clarksburg & Weston Electric / Monongahela Valley Traction, Pickens & Hacker Valley, Pickens & Webster Springs, West Virginia Midland, Strouds Creek & Muddlety and others) 12x. Waypoints are Nominatim geocodes, type-checked, with hand pins where Nominatim returned a road, stream, dam or a wrong town. Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals. despike was tested on and off: no difference on any line (no real hairpin cut).
not_yet_sourced: End years that are the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end ([OPEN]): B&O Clarksburg - Weston 1919 (gone by 30 Sept 1951; the 1923 Clarksburg - Richwood charter may extend it if its route is confirmed); B&O Richwood Branch Weston - Burnsville 1914 (1919 probable by route inference; abandoned 1940s, ICC Finance Docket would date it); B&O Richwood Branch Burnsville - Camden-on-Gauley and Camden-on-Gauley - Richwood 1951 (Grafton - Richwood trains 135/136 still running 30 Sept 1951, end not found); B&O Flatwoods - Sutton 1917 (abandoned 1931).

Start-year brackets: WV&P Gauley Division drawn from 1893, the first confirmed passenger year; track reached Camden-on-Gauley in 1892. Newlon - Pickens drawn from 1893; rail reached Pickens Sept 1892.

Opening-date conflicts recorded, not used: wvncrails has Sutton reached in 1898 and Burnsville in 1892 against 1891 newspapers and timetables; an abandonedonline C&O page has the WV&P 'formed' by a B&O agreement in Dec 1899 against the Sept 1899 timetable heading change; Weston - Burnsville '20 miles' (1891 newspaper) against about 25 (Fowler).
Corporate merger date conflict (1912 per Wikipedia / wvncrails vs 31 Dec 1990 per abandonedonline); does not affect drawing.
Whether Clarksburg - Weston and Weston - Buckhannon were still narrow gauge in Nov 1890 (standard-gauged 1891-92 per abandonedonline); does not affect drawing.
Fowler's 'c' mark on Burnsville Gauley Line Station is undefined in the B&O legend.
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh is an estimate.
branches_deliberately_omitted: Clarksburg, Weston & Glenville (narrow gauge, Clarksburg - Weston from Sept 1879) and Buckhannon & West Fork / Weston & Buckhannon (narrow gauge, Weston - Buckhannon from c.1883): separate predecessor companies whose 1879-1890 passenger service was not researched; need their own report.
Buckhannon River Lumber Co. (narrow gauge, 1886): lumber line, no passenger evidence.
Holly River & Addison / West Virginia Midland (Holly Jct - Webster Springs): a separate company with its own passenger trains; not WV&P.
Pickens & Hacker's Valley and Pickens & Addison (Fowler tables 143 and 142): separate logging roads beyond Pickens; not WV&P.
Strouds Creek & Muddlety (Allingdale - Tioga): a separate company the B&O acquired later; needs its own pass.
Williams River, Cherry River Boom & Lumber and Gauley River branches off Cowen / Gauley Jct: coal and lumber lines with no passenger evidence found.
Ohio River Railroad and Monongahela River Railroad (Camden's other roads): separate companies with their own reports.
B&O Tygart Jct - Buckhannon and the Hampton - Adrian Jct connection used by the 1951 Richwood train: B&O lines, not WV&P; belong in the B&O report.
freight_only_excluded: Weston - Burnsville after the last confirmed passenger year (1914) to its 1940s abandonment.
Clarksburg - Weston after 1919; in Sept 1951 'Rail-Freight Service operated on this branch' with buses (Table 54), freight to 1989-1999.
Burnsville - Richwood after 1951 and Buckhannon - Pickens after 15 Nov 1958 (freight to 1990 / 1992 and later; Hampton - Alexander is today's Beech Mountain RR).

segments.note: Clarksburg (WV&P Junction with the B&O main stem) - West Clarksburg - Mount Clare - Lost Creek - Jane Lew - Fishers Summit - Weston, under the West Virginia & Pittsburg RR. Start 1890: the WV&P 'TIME CARD. To take effect Saturday, Nov. 8, 1890' (Busy Bee, Buckhannon, 23 Jan 1891); Fowler marks Skidmores, Bond Summit and Brick Church '1/1891G'. The line had carried passengers since 1879 under the narrow-gauge Clarksburg, Weston & Glenville, a separate road not drawn here. Two to three trains each way (Clarksburg Telegram 1893-1896 cards). Rule 4 split: the WV&P era ends at the 31 Aug 1899 lease to the Baltimore and Ohio (the same 'June 4, 1899' card is headed WV&P in the Webster Echo of 8 Sep 1899 and 'Baltimore and Ohio Railroad (West Virginia & Pittsburg Division)' by 22 Sep 1899); the B&O feature on the same geometry carries 1899 on. Headway is an estimate from the number of trains the cited cards show, NOT a computed figure.
sources: Segment-level: Busy Bee 23 Jan 1891 p3 and 3 Jul 1891 p2 (WV&P cards); Clarksburg Telegram 21 Jul 1893 p8; Webster Echo 8 Sep 1899 p4 (last WV&P-headed card); Fowler table 18. Headway and avg_speed_kmh NOT sourced.

segments.note: Newlon - Arvondale - Pickens. Rail reached Pickens in September 1892 (Busy Bee 30 Sep 1892, 'just completed to Pickens'), but the first confirmed passenger year is 1893: Busy Bee 28 Apr and 23 Jun 1893 print Newlon - Pickens with times, and the Clarksburg Telegram of 21 Jul 1893 has 'Leave Buckhannon for Pickens 7:10 a.m. and 1:50 p.m.'. Fowler: Pickens 'z' (1893). Through Weston - Pickens trains ran by 1898. The Pickens & Hacker's Valley and Pickens & Addison ran ON from Pickens; they are separate roads, not drawn. Rule 4 split: the WV&P era ends at the 31 Aug 1899 lease to the Baltimore and Ohio (the same 'June 4, 1899' card is headed WV&P in the Webster Echo of 8 Sep 1899 and 'Baltimore and Ohio Railroad (West Virginia & Pittsburg Division)' by 22 Sep 1899); the B&O feature on the same geometry carries 1899 on. segments.note: Weston - Brown's - Rohrbough - Roanoke - Arnold - Peterson - Confluence - Orlando - Burnsville - Coger's - Rollyson - Heater's - Flatwoods: the WV&P main line, built toward Sutton and diverted toward the Gauley at Flatwoods in 1892. Start 1891: Wheeling Intelligencer 16 Feb 1891, 'track laid and ballasted as far as Burnsville'; the WV&P card in the Busy Bee of 3 Jul 1891 has a 'SUTTON DIVISION' Weston - Burnsville - Flat Woods - McNutt's - Sutton with times; Morgantown New Dominion 3 Oct 1891 has the line complete 'forty-three miles from Weston to Sutton'. Through Clarksburg - Camden-on-Gauley trains by 1898 (card of 4 June 1899, 'CLARKSBURG AND CAMDEN-ON-GAULEY'). CONFLICT recorded, not used: wvncrails says the WV&P first reached Burnsville in 1892. Distance conflict recorded: the Feb 1891 paper says 'Burnsville, 20 miles', Fowler about 25. Rule 4 split: the WV&P era ends at the 31 Aug 1899 lease to the Baltimore and Ohio (the same 'June 4, 1899' card is headed WV&P in the Webster Echo of 8 Sep 1899 and 'Baltimore and Ohio Railroad (West Virginia & Pittsburg Division)' by 22 Sep 1899); the B&O feature on the same geometry carries 1899 on. Headway is an estimate from the number of trains the cited cards show, NOT a computed figure.

segments.note: Flatwoods - McNutt's - Karl's Siding - Sutton. Built in 1891 as the end of the WV&P main line; it became a branch when the main line was turned off at Flat Woods toward the Gauley (Wheeling Register 25 Jul 1892). Start 1891: same evidence as the Sutton Division (Busy Bee 3 Jul 1891 card); Fowler marks McNutt, Karl's Siding and Sutton 'z'. The 12 May 1895 and 10 July 1898 cards show a Sutton - Flatwoods shuttle connecting with main-line trains; June 1895 Camden camp-meeting excursion, '200 on the Sutton line' (Webster Echo 14 Jun 1895). CONFLICT recorded, not used: wvncrails says rails reached Sutton in 1898 (OpenHistoricalMap also dates the branch from 1898). Rule 4 split: the WV&P era ends at the 31 Aug 1899 lease to the Baltimore and Ohio (the same 'June 4, 1899' card is headed WV&P in the Webster Echo of 8 Sep 1899 and 'Baltimore and Ohio Railroad (West Virginia & Pittsburg Division)' by 22 Sep 1899); the B&O feature on the same geometry carries 1899 on. Headway is an estimate from the number of trains the cited cards show, NOT a computed figure.

segments.note: Flatwoods - Gillespie - Holly Jct (Palmer Jct) - Centralia - Erbacon - Hardwood - Cowen - Camden-on-Gauley.
